raw_response:
I'll think this through like I do every spring, figuring out my 20 mu.

My 20 mu — I've been doing wheat-maize on most of it for many years because that rotation is steady and the county knows it well. I keep about 14 mu for wheat-maize double cropping, 3 mu for cotton on the sandier strip near the road, and 3 mu for chili because the vegetable buyer from Handan still comes and chili brings cash money when wheat prices are poor.

**Winter wheat (14 mu):** Last year I got about 480 kg/mu. The dealer in town sells Jimai 22 seed, I'll use that again — my neighbor Old Zhang got over 500 kg/mu with it. Base fertilizer I'll broadcast compound 15-15-15 at about 50 kg/mu before ploughing, then urea topdress at green-up. That gives roughly N 16 kg, P 8 kg, K 7 kg per mu. I irrigate with my well — once before winter (dong shui), once at green-up, once at jointing, once at grain filling. Four times. Spray for aphids and wheat rust 2 times usually. I rotary till after maize — no time to deep plough between crops.

**Summer maize (14 mu):** Plant right after wheat harvest, Zhengdan 958 hybrid. N 15 kg/mu (urea at big trumpet stage is the key one), P 6, K 6. Two irrigations if rain is short, one spray for corn borer. Rotary, no-till is what some younger folks try but I don't trust it yet on my ground. Expected 550 kg/mu.

**Cotton (3 mu):** Cotton price is uncertain but I keep it for habit and because that piece of land doesn't do well for wheat. Improved Bt variety from the dealer. N 13 kg, P 6, K 9 — cotton needs potassium for the bolls. Irrigate 3 times. Spray 5 times for bollworm and aphids, cotton is pest-heavy. Plough before planting. Expected 260 kg/mu seed cotton.

**Chili (3 mu):** This is the cash crop, so I spend more. Hybrid seed, about N 18 kg, P 10 kg, K 18 kg — chili eats a lot of potassium. Irrigate 5 times through the season. Spray 6 times — aphids, thrips, anthracnose. Plough and make ridges. Expected 2000 kg/mu fresh.

I'd rather put a little extra fertilizer than come up short — one bad harvest hurts more than a few extra bags of urea.
